queries.hook: A fire lit by choosing your own path; the resolve to stay alive in it, even when the money stops and no one is watching.
queries.diagnose: Resolve fades when the mind runs ahead to the prize or looks sideways at the old life; it holds when the work itself is the reward.
queries.steady: No honest effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.
queries.act: Rise and act; do your work fully and well each day, let the result go, and keep at it when no one is watching.
queries.story: A young warrior who set out to win what was theirs to win, faced the first setback, and kept their resolve through it.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् । सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः ॥
verse.line: Don't abandon work that suits you just because it has flaws. Every undertaking has some, like fire has smoke.
verse.translation: One should not give up the work suited to one's nature, Kaunteya, even if it has faults; for all undertakings are clouded by faults, as fire is by smoke.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.misuse: Not 'never change jobs'. It answers perfectionism, not a reason to stay where you're harmed.

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield, knowing they are afraid to act. He tells them that the work which fits their nature will always have its rough edges. He compares these flaws to smoke around a fire, saying it is not a reason to walk away. He asks them to stay with the work that belongs to them, offering it fully even with its imperfections.
verse.for_you: You are building your own brand, and it is yours. The days will not always feel electric. When the hard days come and the work feels heavy, do not abandon it. Stay with the work that fits you, flaws and all, and offer it to the life you are making.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verse.sanskrit: पुरुषार्थात्फलप्राप्तिर्देशकालवशादिह । प्राप्ता चिरेण शीघ्रं वा यासौ दैवमिति स्मृता ॥
verse.line: Effort brings results, sooner or later, depending on time and place. That timing is what we call fate.
verse.translation: Results come from effort, sooner or later, depending on place and time. That arrival of the fruit, early or late, is what people call fate.
verse.why: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

prasang.title: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort
prasang.summary: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.
prasang.lesson: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha speaks to the young Rama, who is grieving his fate. He tells him that what people call fate is only the result of past effort, arriving on its own schedule. He says Rama should not torment himself over what was never in his hands, but trust that his present effort is already shaping tomorrow.
verse.for_you: Yesterday's verse named the grip. Today, trust the work. The money and the results are coming, but not on your clock. Let go of the anxious need to control the outcome, and trust that your effort is already building the foundation.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
verse.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
verse.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari speaks to the reader from a place of deep steadiness, telling them to let the world praise or blame, let fortune come or go. He says the steadfast do not step off the right path, no matter what happens. He compares them to the gods who kept churning the ocean through poison to find nectar.
verse.for_you: Let the money come or go, let people praise or blame. You are building something new, and the path will have its rough patches. Keep going on the path that is yours. The steady work will carry you through.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: कुर्वतो नार्थसिद्धिर्मे भवतीति ह भारत / निर्वेदो नात्र गन्तव्यो द्वावन्तौ यस्य कर्मणः
verse.line: Don't despair because effort hasn't paid off yet. Every attempt can go either way.
verse.translation: 'I keep working and still don't succeed' is no reason to despair. Every effort can end two ways, in success or not; only by not acting is the outcome certain.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.meaning: Draupadi speaks to Yudhishthira in the forest. They have lost their kingdom and sit in waiting. She tells him that waiting for fate is no plan. She says that saying 'I keep working and still don't succeed' is no reason to despair. Every effort can end two ways, in success or not. Only by not acting is the outcome certain. She asks him to do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on him.
verse.for_you: Your fire is real and it belongs to you. The days will come when the work feels heavy and the money does not show up. When that happens, do not step off the path because the result is missing. Do the work because it is yours, and let the outcome take care of itself.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
verse.line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
verse.translation: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.
verse.misuse: This is not 'don't care about results' or 'don't plan'. Care, plan and aim well; just don't let the outcome own you.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield, where Arjuna is frozen by grief and doubt about the war ahead. Krishna tells him to drop the obsession with victory or defeat and simply do the work before him. The verse proposes that you have a right only to the action itself, not to the outcome. The reward belongs to the doing, not to the winning.
verse.for_you: You are building something new. Do the one small thing that moves your brand forward today. Let go of checking if it is working yet.

verse.speaker: Vidura
verse.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verse.sanskrit: निश्चित्य यः प्रक्रमते नान्तर्वसति कर्मणः / अवन्ध्यकालो वश्यात्मा स वै पण्डित उच्यते
verse.line: Decide, then begin. Don't stall halfway, don't waste time, and keep yourself steady.
verse.translation: One who begins only after deciding, does not stop halfway through the work, does not waste time and keeps himself in hand, is called wise.
verse.why: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

verse.meaning: Vidura, the king's wise brother, speaks to the sleepless King Dhritarashtra on the eve of a peace talk. Vidura tells him that a wise person decides calmly and then acts without stopping halfway or wasting time. The verse proposes that real wisdom is steady action after a clear choice, without stalling.
verse.for_you: Yesterday's verse named the grip on results. Today, decide what you will build tomorrow and begin. Do not let the day pass without one steady step.

story.title: Hanuman's leap
story.story_hook: Halfway across the ocean, a golden mountain rose out of the water and offered him a place to rest.
story.summary: Hanuman leaps across the ocean. A mountain rises to repay an old kindness by offering rest; he thanks it but keeps his promise not to stop. He outwits Surasa by shrinking small and defeats Simhika, and the watching beings praise his steadiness, sight, judgement and skill.
story.lesson: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.

anchor.speaker: Beings of the sky
anchor.setting: Having outwitted two monsters mid-flight, Hanuman is praised by those watching from the sky.
anchor.sanskrit: यस्य त्वेतानि चत्वारि वानरेन्द्र यथा तव। धृतिर्दृष्टिर्मतिर्दाक्ष्य स कर्मसु न सीदति ॥
anchor.line: Steadiness, clear sight, good judgement and skill. With these four, you won't sink at work.
anchor.translation: Whoever has these four, as you do, chief of monkeys, never sinks in his work: steadiness, clear sight, judgement and skill.
anchor.why: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.

prasang.title: Hanuman's leap
prasang.summary: Hanuman leaps across the ocean. A mountain rises to repay an old kindness by offering rest; he thanks it but keeps his promise not to stop. He outwits Surasa by shrinking small and defeats Simhika, and the watching beings praise his steadiness, sight, judgement and skill.
prasang.story_hook: Halfway across the ocean, a golden mountain rose out of the water and offered him a place to rest.
prasang.lesson: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.

story.hook_title: Halfway across the ocean, a mountain rose up and offered Hanuman a rest
story.teaser: Halfway across the ocean, a mountain rose up and offered Hanuman a rest
story.for_you: Yesterday's verse named the grip. Today, look at the fire inside you. Hanuman did not stop to rest on the golden mountain because he knew his leap was his own promise. When the work feels hard, let your steadiness be the mountain you build on, not the comfort you refuse.

script: You are awake right now in a way that feels rare. You left a job last week and the air feels different. You want to protect this fire before the hard days arrive.
Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield. Arjuna is frozen, afraid to move. Krishna looks at the smoke and weapons around them and says: And Krishna replied:
सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत्, सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः.
In plain words: Don't abandon work that suits you just because it has flaws. Every undertaking has some, like fire has smoke.

This is harder than it sounds. It is easy to quit when the work gets heavy or the path looks messy. But every undertaking has smoke. The fire is your work, and the smoke is the flaw. You do not leave the fire because of the smoke. You offer the work as it is.
Your brand is yours. When the days feel flat, do not abandon the work. Offer it as it is, flaws and all.

depth.life: You are building your own brand, and it is yours. The days will not always feel electric. When the hard days come and the work feels heavy, do not abandon it. Stay with the work that fits you, flaws and all, and offer it to the life you are making.
depth.points: Every path has its smoke. Perfectionism is the trap. The Gita tells you to stay with what is yours to build, not because it is perfect, but because it is yours.
depth.practice: When the work feels heavy today, name one flaw and one reason you are staying anyway.
depth.question: What is the one flaw you can name right now?
